observations: body L1, L3, L6, L8, L13, L19, L24: the dashes of the transliterated names and titles and of «41–44» and «170–172» are long dashes (4.4 to 5.3 pt); in L3 «al-Mas‘ūdī» has a hyphen (3.3 pt).
body L14: the dash at the head of the line measures 10.0 pt and is transcribed as a dash.
body L1-L4: 1° in 100 years is 36″ a year, a sign in 3000 years and the whole ecliptic in 36000.
body L6-L10: 387 revolutions of the apogee in the kalpa of 4 320 000 000 years give one in 11 162 790,7 years and 1′ in 516,8 years; one revolution in 9 000 000 years gives 1′ in 416,66... years.
body L24: 16° 47′ is the difference between al-Battānī's 82° 17′ and Ptolemy's 65° 30′.
body L21: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXIV; AB01-PDF0441-body-L021) read 12″ 12/299 for the printed 11″ 12/299: 3600″ : 299 = 12″ 12/299 a year. The printed number is kept.
notes_left L13-L23: the long vowels of the English titles and quotation are marked with circumflexes, as by Thibaut; that of the i of «Dvivedî» is printed as a single stroke.
notes_left L22-L24: at the head of these lines the guillemets and the first letters of «tise», «that» and «form» have slipped and stand askew.

notes_left L1, L5, notes_right L6-L7, L10-L11, L20-L21: the dashes of «Al-Bīrūnī», «as-Sindhind», «karaṇa-writer», «211-212», «18-19», «Pulisa-siddhānta», «’l-ḥasan», «109-111» and «az-Zarqālī» measure 2.5 to 4.1 pt, hyphens.
notes_right L18: az-Zarqālī lived in the 11th century (p. 214: posteriore XI saec. Chr. medietate); the print has «X Chr. saeculo».
notes_right L23: the signature 28 stands at the foot of the page, below the right column of the notes.
notes_right L17-L18: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXIV; AB01-PDF0441-body-L021) read XI for the X of «fuit X Chr. saeculo»; the printed X is kept.

transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
